stem.en: Two blocks P and Q are on a smooth, level surface. Two forces act on block P: 5 N in one direction and 4 N in the opposite direction. Block Q moves with a constant velocity. Which statement is correct?

text.en: Q has a net force on it, and P does not.

feedback.en: Q moves with a constant velocity, so the net force on Q is zero.

text.en: Both P and Q have a net force on them.

feedback.en: Q moves with a constant velocity, so no net force acts on it.

text.en: Neither P nor Q has a net force on it.

feedback.en: On P, 5 N - 4 N = 1 N. That is a net force.

text.en: P has a net force on it, and Q does not.

feedback.en: Right. On P, the net force is 5 N - 4 N = 1 N. Q has a constant velocity, so its net force is zero.

explanation.en: On P the forces do not balance: the net force is 5 N - 4 N = 1 N. Q moves with a constant velocity, so by the first law the net force on it is zero.

hints.en: Find the net force on P first. Then ask: does the velocity of Q change?
